title: Users
intro: Every user is a Linux account of its own, so files they create belong to them. Their uids are never given out again.

field.usernameHint: Lowercase letters, digits, hyphens and underscores, starting with a letter or underscore.
field.groupsHint: Every user is also in the group users.

create.title: Create user
create.intro: The user gets a home folder on the first pool when there is one.

password.title: New password for {name}
password.intro: The user is signed out everywhere and signs in with the new password.
password.fileServices: SMB and SFTP use the new password as well.

delete.title: Delete {name}?
delete.intro: The account goes. The user's files and home folder stay, and the user id is never given to anyone else.

fileServices.title: File services
fileServices.signInOnce: Not ready for SMB and SFTP yet: the user signs in once on the web, or you set a new password.

groups.title: Groups
groups.intro: Every group is a Linux group of its own; its group id is never given out again. Rights given to a group apply to all its members.
groups.builtinDescription: Every user is a member. It cannot be changed.

create.title: Create group
create.intro: Users can be in any number of groups.

delete.title: Delete group {name}?
delete.intro: The group goes; its members stay. Files keep the group id, and it is never given to another group.
delete.label: Delete group {name}

grants.userIntro: The user has these rights and everything its groups give it. There are no rules that take a right away.
grants.groupIntro: Every member has these rights, besides its own and those of its other groups.
grants.noShares: There are no shared folders yet.
grants.adminHasAll: Administrators have every right and reach every shared folder.

right.sshLogin: Sign in over SSH with a shell
